notes: THE golden for the no-model surfer: a prompt addressed to a corpus must snip the segment it addresses — omnilingual, omnigenre, byte-accurate.

Each case is a document set, a prompt, and the segment label (or typed gap) that prompt MUST return. Scored by scripts/score-surfer-golden.mjs; a conformance test asserts every case passes on every npm test.

The surfer is deterministic host code, so unlike the emergent span-golden (a ceiling tracker) this golden is a 100% contract: any FAIL is a regression, and a re-earned engine must re-score green before it ships.

Frozen BEFORE engine changes. Re-score with one command (node scripts/score-surfer-golden.mjs); only deliberately amended cases may move, and the LIVE baseline in the scorer header is rewritten only by an amendment.

Fixtures: the English novel body is the real pg84 (Frankenstein) opening; the remaining non-English bodies are fixture prose. The golden tests FORMS — a heading's shape, its numeral script, its address — not quotation, so fixture prose is honest material.

Numeral policy: ASCII digits carry intrinsic value (chapter 18 finds CHAPTER XVIII, psalm ii finds PSALM II); roman converts both ways; non-ASCII digit scripts (Devanagari, Arabic-Indic) address by their own surface and never across scripts — crossing a digit script is a value claim, and value claims are priors (eoPriors), never an engine guess.

Accent policy: case and Latin accents fold through the single-pass diaNorm map (perceiver/text/surfaces.js — never a third map). Greek tonos folding is a language prior, so the Greek case addresses by the accentless surface a printed heading actually carries.
CJK and any spaced-script content need a word-segmentation prior: the Chinese case is pinned to its typed gap until that prior lands, then the case is amended with the segment it unlocks.

Ordinals (the second chapter) are prior vocabulary, not form: they fall through to the content phase, where they are matched as tokens or missed as a typed gap. They are deliberately not enshrined as a pass here.
The flat outline cannot tell two same-labelled segments apart: ambiguity is a typed gap that cites the byte coordinates, never a coin flip.

source:frankenstein.txt.text:
Letter 1

_To Mrs. Saville, England._

St. Petersburgh, Dec. 11th, 17—.

You will rejoice to hear that no disaster has accompanied the commencement of an enterprise which you have regarded with such evil forebodings. I arrived here yesterday, and my first task is to assure my dear sister of my welfare and increasing confidence in the success of my undertaking.

Letter 2

I am already far north of London, and as I walk in the streets of Petersburgh, I feel a cold northern breeze play upon my cheeks, which braces my nerves and fills me with delight. Do you understand this feeling? This breeze, which has travelled from the regions towards which I am advancing, gives me a foretaste of those icy climes.

Chapter 1

I am by birth a Genevese, and my family is one of the most distinguished of that republic. My ancestors had been for many years counsellors and syndics, and my father had filled several public situations with honour and reputation. He was respected by all who knew him for his integrity and indefatigable attention to public business.

Chapter 2

We were brought up together; there was not quite a year difference in our ages. I need not say that we were strangers to any species of disunion or dispute. Harmony was the soul of our companionship, and the diversity and contrast that subsisted in our characters drew us nearer together.

source:voyna.txt.text:
ЧАСТЬ ПЕРВАЯ

Это был вечер в петербургском салоне; разговор шёл о войне и о политике, и хозяйка дома едва успевала следить за всеми гостями.

ГЛАВА I

В июле 1805 года в Петербурге у Анны Павловны Шерер собралось общество, о котором говорил весь город. Собрание наполнилось постепенно, и каждый гость входил с тем выражением, какое полагалось приличием.

ГЛАВА II

Гостиная Анны Павловны начала понемногу наполняться. Приехала высшая знать Петербурга, люди самые разнородные по возрастам и характерам, но одинаковые по обществу, в котором все они жили.
